results.name: 1a · no painted text on the Play tab trails off
results.detail: 230 painted text leaves scanned across the turn options, the reactions band, the deck and every mounted dialog — none ends in an ellipsis

results.name: 1b · and nothing is cutting itself off in CSS either  <-- finding Q
results.detail: no painted leaf overflows its own box with text-overflow:ellipsis or a line-clamp. This is the half textContent cannot see: CSS-clipped text reports in FULL to a string renderer, so every node-side "no ellipsis" test in this repo is blind to it

results.name: 2a · every option row is the same height, and none is clipped
results.detail: 3 rows, height 56px, 3/3 fit their own box. A uniform row is what makes the list scannable mid-turn; "fits" is the half that distinguishes a two-line row from a three-line row with the third line cut off

results.name: 2b · one tap opens the full definition, and it is long-form prose
results.detail: «Longsword — details» → a painted dialog 390×760 carrying 3759 characters, no trailing ellipsis. The row is the glance; this is the route the phase was opened to build

results.name: 2c · and nothing inside the opened sheet trails off either
results.detail: the surface that carries the LONGEST text in the app is the one most likely to cut it, and it cuts nothing

results.name: 3 · all four are painted and inside the unscrolled window
results.detail: Save DC="14Save DC"  AC="18AC"  Init="+1Init"  Prof="+3Prof"  — main is the bounded scroll region y=56..411, and every cell sits inside it at scrollY=0. "Without scrolling" is a claim about the WINDOW, not about the document, which is why it is measured against main and not against innerHeight

results.name: 3b · and they are the numbers off his sheet, not placeholders
results.detail: DC 14 (8+3+3 with CHA 16), AC 18, Init +1 (DEX 12), Prof +3 (level 7) — computed from the seeded sheet, and every one of them matches what Marcus reported on 2026-08-27

results.name: 4a · the list exists and carries more than one reaction
results.detail: 5 rows: Sentinel · takes the Disengage action | Sentinel · attacks a target other than you | Interception | Opportunity Attack — Longsword | Flaming Cloak

results.name: 4b · every row states WHEN before it states the dice
results.detail: Sentinel · takes the Disengage action: when@46 dice@-1 | Sentinel · attacks a target other than you: when@51 dice@-1 | Interception: when@21 dice@155 | Opportunity Attack — Longsword: when@39 dice@96 | Flaming Cloak: when@33 dice@89  — a reaction you cannot use is a number; the trigger is the whole of what makes it a choice

results.name: 4c · and the cloak's retaliation says it is FREE  <-- his own misreading, corrected
results.detail: «10 temp HP · 1d10 Fire retaliation (free)» — Marcus believed the 1d10 costs his Reaction. Canon prices the ACTIVATION (Reaction · 1 Channel Divinity use) and leaves the retaliation free, automatic and uncapped. Both facts are on this one row

results.name: 4a2 · every reaction row wears its own heading, and every heading is readable
results.detail: 5 rows, 5 distinct headings, 0 unreadable: «Sentinel · takes the Disengage action» «Sentinel · attacks a target other than you» «Interception» «Opportunity Attack — Longsword» «Flaming Cloak»  — finding BJ: one feat with two reaction clauses now heads each row with its own trigger words, lifted verbatim from canon at the point the two triggers stop agreeing, so «Sentinel» twice became «Sentinel · takes the Disengage action» and «Sentinel · attacks a target other than you». Both rows survive — nothing was collapsed to make this pass

results.name: 4d · reachable from the deck — the deck names Reaction as a thing you spend
results.detail: the fixed deck (390×368 at y=412) carries a painted Reaction pip, and the band sits in the same scroll region above it

results.name: 5a · the deck folds, and gets smaller doing it
results.detail: deck 368px → 252px, and the control now reads "Expand turn deck". The height is the claim: aria-expanded="false" over an unchanged box is a lie a screen reader believes and Marcus does not

results.name: 5b · and the spend state survives the fold  <-- the whole point of folding it
results.detail: 7 painted spend pips with the deck folded: Action, Bonus, Move, Action, Bonus, Reaction, Move. A deck that hides whether you have used your Action is a deck you have to unfold every round, which is not a minimise

results.name: 5c · Active Conditions opens and closes, and the box moves with it
results.detail: aria-expanded false → true, container 57px → 495px. Marcus asked for this one by name: "it doesnt happen often and that portion takes up so much room"

results.name: 6a · the SHIPPED bundle names no Gemini model at all
results.detail: zero model ids in dist/. The 404 Marcus hit was models/gemini-2.0-flash, hardcoded in six places; the model is now resolved by asking Google's own /models endpoint and ranking the answer by SHAPE (newest flash > flash-lite > pro). Google can retire anything and the app follows without a deploy — which is the actual requirement, not "it worked once"

results.name: 6b · the settings screen offers a key, a test, and an AUTOMATIC model
results.detail: key field true, Test Connection true, "Automatic" offered true. Automatic is the default because a default that names a model is a default with a shelf life

results.name: 6c · UNVERIFIED: that Gemini actually connects with Marcus's key
results.detail: This needs his private API key and a live round trip to Google, which is 🟡 ASK-FIRST (spend money / exceed an API cap) and is not something a prover may do unasked. What IS proved: 49 unit tests in ai.test.ts cover the resolve-rank-retry path including a simulated retirement, and the shipped bundle names no model. What is NOT proved: that his key is valid and his quota is live. He settles that in ten seconds by tapping Test Connection.

results.name: 7 · tests, types and build — measured by npx vitest run, not by this prover
results.detail: Must read: 968 passed + 7 skipped across 41 files, tsc --noEmit clean, npm run build ✓. Includes storage-safety.test.tsx tests 25 and 26 (both storage keys byte-identical across a full render, and nothing reached for the pen), format.test.ts test 7 (no row line contains an ellipsis in any form, across all 71 canon spells) and test 8 (no line exceeds the 46-char two-line budget), and tactics.test.ts (rejoining every bullet of all 71 records returns the input character for character). Those four are where "all 71" is actually asserted — a browser can only ever see the spells one character happens to know.

results.name: 8a · reading the tab — a definition, a fold, a retaliation — never touches the sheet
results.detail: 6753 bytes in, 6753 bytes out, identical to the seed. Recording a retaliation is the one worth naming: it is this phase's newest write, and it landed entirely on codex-combat-nix-fixture, which is the only key this tab owns

results.name: 8b · and the interactions really happened, so 8a is not passing by doing nothing
results.detail: codex-combat-nix-fixture changed while the sheet did not — the two-writer bug class this phase opened against, measured at the end of it. Without this line 8a would read just as green against a tab where every button was dead

results.name: 8c · spending a slot changes the slot he spent, and nothing else on his sheet
results.detail: 6 paths moved and every one is accounted for: spellSlots.1.current, updatedAt, identities, customHooks, resourcePools, customConditions. The slot went 3→2, which is the tap. 4 of the rest are the loader adding empty optional arrays — additive, lossless, and present on any save from any tab. NOTHING was removed and no other value moved, which is the actual content of "except for anything Marcus himself chose to change"
